title: Prescience
summary: PRESCIENCE, noun presi'ence or pre'shens. [Low Latin proescientia; proe, before, and scientia, knowledge.] Foreknowledge; knowledge of events before they take place. Absolute prescience belongs to God

inlines.v: PRESCIENCE, noun presi'ence or pre'shens. [Low Latin proescientia; proe, before, and scientia, knowledge.] Foreknowledge; knowledge of events before they take place. Absolute prescience belongs to God only. Of things of the most accidental and mutable nature, God's prescience is certain.
